messages:
alex: quick heads-up — after flipping FA v3 on the transformers-llama config in the canary pool, we saw small but consistent memory bumps and a weird latency blip on short seqs (~2–6ms p95). throughput for long seqs improves as expected tho.

marta: ugh. observed the same in my local perf run. memory resident set size went up ~120MB on a 16GB worker for seq_len=64 workloads.

nikhil: do we have the perf-bot nightly dump for that commit? can we point at a revision?

perf-bot: nightly-bench: commit 7f3a2b9, model: llama-13b, config: flashattn-v3-enabled, p95 latency short-seq: +4.3ms, p95 latency long-seq: -12ms, gpu_mem_usage: +118MB. link: https://bench/redwood/18025/7f3a2b9

chao: interesting — my hypothesis is extra workspace padding in the v3 kernels. FA v3 aligns to 128-byte segments for tensor ops which can blow up the temporary buffer for short batches.

alex: that matches what I saw in logs — allocation traces show larger "workspace" allocations around attention callsites. Not OOM, just noisier.

rachel: can you paste the minimal repro args? I can run an isolated kernel trace on a dev instance.

alex: repro command i used: 
```
python -m rti.run --model llama-13b --batch_size 2 --seq_len 64 --use-flashattn v3 --workspace-pool=on
```
noticed the bump when workspace-pool fragmentation happens (many different shape combos).

marta: tried toggling `workspace-pool` to `strict` and the bump disappeared but latency on long seqs regressed slightly. so there's a tradeoff.

nikhil: maybe we can add a kernel selector heuristic: if seq_len < 128 and batch_size <= 4, force FA v2-like compact workspace path (or a fallback) to avoid the padding penalty. Could be a runtime toggle.

chao: yes — implementable. v3 has an API param for `compact_mode` in our fork. We could expose an alignment threshold in kernel selection: prefer compact when pad_overhead_ratio > 0.15.

alex: sounds good. two follow-ups: 1) measure exact pad_overhead_ratio distribution across real traffic (prod traces), 2) add a canary that toggles compact_mode via routing policy per model.

rachel: i'll run trace aggregation across last 7 days and send histograms. if most requests are short, we need compact default.

perf-bot: quick note — our nightly also shows increased CPU host-side memcpy for short sequences with v3, likely memory-copying more tiny slices.

marta: ok. plan: (1) rachel posts histograms, (2) chao adds a kernel selector patch with env flag `FA_FORCE_COMPACT=1` + metric tags, (3) nikhil wires canary route. assign owners?

alex: i'll own the canary routing. chao take the selector patch? rachel do histograms? marta will own validation runs.

chao: on it. i'll open a small RFC follow-up PR with microbench numbers and a fallback. expecting ~1 day to get a prototype.

rachel: I'll upload histograms to the perf dashboard by EOD. early look: ~62% of requests are seq_len<=64 in the canary pool.

nikhil: if that's true, defaulting to compact for the canary seems reasonable. keep an eye on long-seq customers. we should expose override at model pin config.

marta: also let's add an allocation logging flag to the runtime so we can correlate workspace allocations to model requests without sampling noise. small perf cost but useful for a week.

alex: agreed. I'll add the logging toggle to the canary and enable it.

chao: one more edge: v3's kernel sometimes increases CUDA occupancy for long keys due to extra kernels; our selector should consider both pad overhead and kernel-count overhead. I'll add a simple cost model in PR.

alex: perfect. thx everyone. i'll post a short summary in the eng-runtime channel when the canary is live. :thumbsup:
